verdicts.dateTest: Claim as actor/act/thing/when: World Bank DEC management and Group Internal Audit reviewed every post-Bank-wide-review data change in DB2016 to DB2020 (published Oct 2015 to Oct 2019) and confirmed nine irregularities in four countries. DEC's review is dated 2020-12-16, GIA's verification Report FY21-2-4-2104615 is dated 2020-12-08, and WilmerHale's report is dated 2021-09-15. The dates line up. Both India items (the DB16 Mumbai Getting Electricity change and the DB17 construction-permits concern) come from the NDA period, which began May 2014, and both fall inside the review window. Scope gap: DB2015 (Oct 2014, India at 142) is outside the review, and so is anything that happened before Bank-wide review, such as government-submitted data or methodology redesign. 'Not among the irregularities' is true only inside that scope.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The GIA table names 'India (Mumbai) Getting Electricity' (DB16), next to Indonesia, Slovakia, Chile and Mexico. It also names 'the treatment of India during DB17 regarding the inconsistent application of the DB data collection methodology for the "Dealing with Construction Permits" indicator.' The nine corrected items are Azerbaijan (3, DB20), Saudi Arabia (2, DB20), UAE (1, DB20) and China (3, marked 'DB 18-20' in the GIA table; DEC's summary puts China's rank effect in DB2018). None of them is India. No person, family or community is framed as the actor.
verdicts.baseRate: 4 of about 190 economies (about 2%) had confirmed irregularities. India was one of 6 flagged-then-cleared items: the five DB16 electricity changes plus the DB17 India methodology concern. Being flagged was common and did not predict a confirmed irregularity. Symmetry holds: the same lens returns a positive finding for China, Saudi Arabia, Azerbaijan and UAE, so it can tell cases apart and is not just clearing a friendly borrower. The UPA/NDA control cannot be applied because DB2015 and earlier are outside the review scope.
verdicts.denialFound: No separate denial found from the Government of India or DPIIT. Contrary-reporting search was not possible because this session's WebSearch budget was used up (200/200), so Indian press or opposition allegations from 2021 went unchecked. The institution's own record serves as the response. GIA: 'DEC management reconfirmed that these changes were not data irregularities as no specific improprieties were identified' (http://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/569901608154479291/txt/Management-Review-of-Data-Irregularities-in-the-Doing-Business-Reports-from-2016-to-2020-Verification-Report.txt). The DEC review (https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/791761608145561083-0050022020/original/DBDataIrregularitiesReviewDec2020.pdf, 21 pp) and the WilmerHale report (https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/84a922cc9273b7b120d49ad3b9e9d3f9-0090012021/original/DB-Investigation-Findings-and-Report-to-the-Board-of-Executive-Directors-September-15-2021.pdf, all 16 pp extracted) contain zero mentions of India.
verdicts.innocentReading: India's rank rose from 142 to 130, 130, 100, 77 and 63 (DB2015 to DB2020). That fits reforms the methodology rewarded (IBC 2016, GST 2017, Delhi/Mumbai permit and electricity single-window reforms) and a two-city (Delhi/Mumbai) sample that a targeted state-level push could move. The two India items were routine data changes and a methodology-consistency question. The DB team raised them itself, and management cleared them.
verdicts.reason: Every quoted element checks out word for word in the GIA text. Two further primary documents confirm the claim. The DEC review names only Azerbaijan, Saudi Arabia, UAE and China, and the WilmerHale report's mandate names the same four countries, with no mention of India anywhere in its text. Calling the narrative 'unsupported' rather than 'debunked' is the right calibration. The review only covered changes made between Bank-wide review and publication. GIA 'did not assess DEC management's technical judgement' and 'did not verify the underlying scoring method', and DB2015 plus anything before review are outside scope. So the record shows no evidence of gaming for India, but it does not prove the rank was clean. The one weak point is that contrary reporting (2021 Indian press or opposition allegations) could not be searched in this session.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Replace 'Wikipedia summary of WilmerHale (not opened here)' in narrative:5 and literature:c021 with the WilmerHale PDF itself (URL above). It is reachable, and its scope paragraph names only China (DB2018) and Saudi Arabia, UAE and Azerbaijan (DB2020), with zero India mentions. 2) Add the DEC review 'Review of Data Irregularities in Doing Business' (2020-12-16, URL above) as a primary source; it has no India mention. 3) Add the scope caveat to strongestCounter: the review covered only post-Bank-wide-review changes in DB16 to DB20. GIA did not assess technical judgement or the scoring method, and DB2015 and methodology redesign are outside scope. 4) Complete the quote: '...not data irregularities as no specific improprieties were identified'. Also state that the DB17 concern was about 'inconsistent application of the DB data collection methodology' and was cleared by management, not tested independently by GIA. 5) In literature:c022, the label '130 (DB2017/18)' is wrong. Wikipedia's table gives India 142 (DB2015), 130 (DB2016), 130 (DB2017), 100 (DB2018), 77 (DB2019), 63 (DB2020), so the label should read 142→130 (DB2016/17)→100 (DB2018)→77→63. 6) 'unsupported' is a narrative status, not a contract tier. The underlying audit facts are tier 'documented'. 7) Add a gap entry: a search for 2021 Indian press or opposition allegations about India's DB rank has not been run.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated, the claim is "GoI had legislated or announced all 26 prior actions of P173943 (PD 2020-04-30), P174292 (PD 2020-06-16) and P181032 (PD 2023-06-02) before appraisal." The count holds: 8, 7 and 11 prior actions, all marked [Achieved] in the matrices. The 2020 dates also hold. PMGKY was announced 2020-03-26 and approved 2020-05-14. P174292 PA5 is dated to the "circular issued on August 13, 2019", and PA7 (PSB59) was "Launched in November 2018". The low-carbon PAs (NGHM Cabinet approval Jan 2023, EC Amendment Act Dec 2022, SEBI GDS amendments Feb 2023, Sovereign Green Bond Framework Nov 2022) were completed before the PD. That is true of every DPF by design, so being dated before approval tells us nothing about who designed a measure. The same PD says the forward triggers were already in the GoI pipeline: "The draft CCTS regulation is under stakeholder consultation". That weakens the claim that the triggers are "the strongest case" of conditionality.
verdicts.identityTest: The project IDs and PD URLs match: P173943 PMGKY DPF1, P174292 MSME Emergency Response DPL, P181032 First Low-Carbon Energy Programmatic DPO. The actor is the IBRD as an institution, not a family or bloodline, so no kill is needed on that ground. The attribution in strongestCounter is wrong, though. "ICR/IEG describe the operations as financing GoI's own programmes (PMGKY, Atmanirbhar, NGHM)" cites the only ICR/IEG source used, which is the IEG ICR Review of P173943/P174027 (the social-protection series). That review has zero occurrences of "hydrogen" or "NGHM" and does not mention Atmanirbhar. No cited ICR or IEG source covers P174292 or P181032.
verdicts.baseRate: Close to 100% of DPF prior actions everywhere are government acts completed before Board approval, because that is the definition of a prior action. So "pre-announced GoI measure" does not discriminate between dictation and non-dictation. The property that does discriminate is Bank TA or co-design of a measure before it is issued. P181032 has that property for at least 4 of its 11 PAs (1, 9, 10, 11) by its own Table 4, and WB studies are listed as the analytical underpinning for PAs 2–7. The UPA-era DPLs (e.g. 2009 Banking Sector Support) are the control in SPEC. They were not tested here, so the symmetry check is incomplete.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Neither GoI (DEA) nor the Bank was asked. The closest thing to a response is in the Bank's own documents. The P181032 PD (para 12) says "At the request of the GoI, the World Bank has been providing significant technical and financing support". The IEG review of P173943 says "The DPFs also reflected the goverment's policies and priorities". Sources: https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099060623092565311/text/BOSIB0342f50d505508c7803e3b35fb5c59.txt ; https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099021425103520204/text/P173943-594240c2-796b-4b0c-80b6-a58ce6d8637c.txt
verdicts.innocentReading: DPF is designed to reward reforms the borrower has already completed. The Bank gives TA on request, and then bundles and prices measures GoI was going to adopt anyway. In 2020 the loans were cheap budget support during a fiscal shock. In 2023 the Bank's TA fed into a GoI decarbonisation agenda (NGHM, carbon market, green bonds) that GoI itself set out in its LT-LEDS (2022). This is co-design at the borrower's request, not dictation.
verdicts.reason:
The narrative's summary leaves out a fact stated in its own cited source, and that fact comes close to meeting the narrative's own falsifier. whatWouldChangeThis asks for "Bank mission records showing drafting before announcement". The P181032 PD's Table 4 ("DPO PAs and Analytical Underpinnings") already says:
- PA9: "WB: Designing carbon market in India through technical assistance on partnership for market readiness … Key findings: Supported BEE in designing the carbon market in India"
- PA10: "Supported SEBI to amend the existing regulations"
- PA11: "Supported the MoF on the design of the Sovereign Green Bond Framework"
Para 10 adds that Bank TA "provided inputs to the National Green Hydrogen Roadmap, the NGHM".
The IEG review also says the climate pillar (the ISTS waiver) was added to a social-protection DPO because it "corresponded with Country Management Unit (CMU) norms to support important climate actions through national DPOs". In other words, the Bank chose which GoI measures to condition on.

So "all 26 prior actions were pre-announced GoI measures" is literally true, but it is presented as a counter to Bank influence when it is not one. The strongest case is not the forward triggers. It is the Bank's documented TA in designing PAs 1, 9, 10 and 11, and both triggers named were already in consultation before the PD.

"Dictates" is still not shown, because the TA was given at GoI request and nothing shows GoI adopting a measure against its will. The narrative therefore survives only in a reworded form, with a corrected strongestCase and strongestCounter.

The 2019–24 scope has two further problems. The second low-carbon DPF (June 2024), where the triggers became prior actions, was not read. P174027's PAs (the Labour Codes) are in the file but are not counted in the 26.
verdicts.corrections:
narratives[0].status: keep "unsupported" only for the word "dictates". Add in strongestCase that "influences the design of" would be "well-supported". Or reword the claim and set the status to "contested".

narratives[0].strongestCase: replace with the PD Table 4 facts. The Bank's own P181032 Program Document credits Bank TA with designing or supporting PA9 (carbon market, via PMR TA to BEE), PA10 (SEBI GDS amendments, via TA under P177285), PA11 (Sovereign Green Bond Framework) and inputs to NGHM (PA1). IEG says the climate pillar in the PMGKY DPOs was added under Bank CMU norms. Keep the US$2.75bn 2020 fiscal-stress point.

narratives[0].strongestCounter: remove "Atmanirbhar, NGHM" from the ICR/IEG attribution, because the cited IEG review covers only P173943/P174027. Change the wording to "GoI measures completed before appraisal (by DPF design); the Bank's TA was provided at GoI request (P181032 PD para 12)".

narratives[0].whatWouldChangeThis: note that Bank co-design before issuance is already documented for 4 PAs. Replace it with "evidence that GoI adopted a measure it had opposed, or that disbursement was withheld pending a measure GoI resisted".

Add the P181032 PD Table 4 quote to srcs. Record in gaps that the DPF2 low-carbon Program Document (June 2024) and the P174027 PAs were not counted.

worldbank:c064: killIf ("drafted with Bank staff before announcement") is partly met for the 2023 PAs by the same PD. Scope c064's conclusion to the 2020 operations only. For P181032, add a separate analytic claim citing Table 4.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: the NDA Union government (from 2014-05-26) did not steer IBRD/IDA board approvals toward BJP-ruled states over 2014-05-26 to 2026-09-26, with UPA (2004-05-22 to 2014-05-25) as the control. The window dates are correct. The weakness is that a board approval date comes after 2 to 4 years of preparation, so loans approved in 2014 to 2016 were prepared under UPA and some state loans were prepared under a previous state government. The narrative applies no lag. Party labels also need fixing. AP's NDA-period money was mostly approved while TDP was an NDA ally: AP Disaster Recovery 2015 (US$250m), 24x7 Power 2017 (US$400m total / US$240m Bank) and Amaravati 2024-12-19 (US$1,600m total / US$800m IBRD). The YSRCP period (2019-05-30 to 2024-06-12) accounts only for SALT (US$250m). Tamil Nadu's AIADMK was a formal NDA ally from 2019-02 to 2023-09. Chhattisgarh was Congress-run 2018-12 to 2023-12 and MP 2018-12 to 2020-03. Kerala was UDF-run 2014 to 2016, not LDF. None of this reverses the verdict, but AP should not be presented as an opposition counter-example.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities are Indian states, matched by a regex on project_name/impagency in the World Bank Projects API v3. I re-fetched the API (1,117 records). The file's NDA totals match exactly: 188 projects, US$49,796m. The UPA totals also match: 177 projects, US$37,496m. The state figures reproduce for Assam (US$2,294m), Gujarat (US$1,630m, once the case-insensitive 'Goa' match in 'GOAL' is fixed), Kerala (US$1,395m), TN (US$2,750m) and AP (US$3,008m). UP does not reproduce: the file says US$2,650m (0.61x), but name, implementing-agency and PDO matching gives about US$1,070m (0.26-0.29x). There is also a currency/entity problem. The file sums curr_total_commitment, which includes co-financiers, and presents it as 'World Bank money'. For Amaravati P507508, curr_total_commitment is 1,600,000,000 but curr_ibrd_commitment is 800,000,000; the other half is non-Bank co-financing. The same applies to GOAL P173704 (750 vs 500 IBRD), Resilient Kerala P174778 (370 vs 125), Chennai P175221 (300 vs 150) and MP Rural Connectivity (350 vs 210).
verdicts.baseRate: Under the NDA, 11 of 25 states are above 1.5x. Seven of those 11 are small hill or north-eastern states with less than 1% of the population each, so a high per-capita ratio mostly reflects state size, not party. I ran my own discriminating test: I coded whether each state was BJP/NDA-aligned on each project's approval date and weighted population by the fraction of 2014-26 each state spent aligned. Aligned states received 58.0% of state-attributed commitments against a 54.9% aligned population-time share, a ratio of 1.06x. On an IBRD+IDA-only basis the figures are 57.8% vs 54.9%, or 1.05x. That is parity, so there is no party-aligned skew. Recomputed on IBRD+IDA only (my denominators): Assam about 3.96x, Gujarat 1.23x, Kerala 1.74x, TN 1.94x, AP 1.30x, UP 0.29x, MP 0.49x, Haryana 0.64x, Chhattisgarh 0.05x. Under UPA the same lens gives HP 9.0x (7.7x on IBRD+IDA only; the file says 9.7x), Odisha 1.84x (file says 2.0x) and Gujarat 0.26x. That confirms the symmetry control required by the SPEC.
verdicts.denialFound: No DEA or World Bank statement addresses state allocation by party, and none was sought: not asked. Related items found: (1) In 2019 the Centre withdrew the Amaravati US$300m request after YSRCP took office, and the Bank dropped the loan (https://scroll.in/latest/931130/world-bank-drops-300-million-loan-proposal-to-develop-amaravati-after-centre-withdraws-request). This fits either reading, because the state was the party that lost interest. (2) On 2025-11-16 Jan Suraaj (Uday Singh, Pavan Verma) alleged that 'Rs 14,000 crore of the loan they received from the World Bank has been diverted for doles' in NDA-run Bihar before the 2025 election (https://newsarenaindia.com/bihar-assembly-election/14-000-cr-world-bank-loan-used-in-bihar-polls-pk-s-party/62342). That is an allegation about how a state used money, not about the Centre steering it, and no response was reported. (3) Kerala's 2024 complaints of Centre discrimination concern borrowing limits and devolution, not World Bank allocation.
verdicts.innocentReading: A state's share of World Bank money depends mainly on four things. First, which states prepare projects: the pipeline takes 2 to 4 years. Second, implementing capacity and the state's FRBM borrowing headroom under Article 293. Third, the Bank's post-2014 shift toward lending to states and PforRs. Fourth, the arithmetic of small hill and north-eastern states, where one US$100-250m project gives a very high per-capita ratio. These explain both the NDA-period and the UPA-period dispersion without any party variable.
verdicts.reason: The claim is that the steering thesis is unsupported, and that verdict survives both lenses. Opposition-run Kerala and TN are above parity, and large BJP-run states (UP, MP, Haryana) are below it. The UPA control produces equally extreme ratios, and an aggregate party-alignment test on approval dates comes out at 1.05-1.06x, i.e. parity. The supporting numbers are flawed but not in a way that helps the steering thesis. The amounts include non-Bank co-financing. The UP figure is not reproducible and is probably overstated, which makes UP even lower. AP is mislabelled as a YSRCP-era counter-example when most of its money came under the TDP-NDA ally. 'Unsupported' is not a contract tier. This is our own inference, so it belongs at analytic with the innocentReading attached.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Set tier to 'analytic' instead of 'unsupported', keep status: unsupported, and attach the innocentReading. 2) Replace 'World Bank money' figures with curr_ibrd_commitment + curr_ida_commitment, or relabel them 'total project commitment incl. co-financing'. Amaravati P507508 should be US$800m IBRD, not US$1,600m; GOAL P173704 US$500m, not 750; Resilient Kerala P174778 US$125m, not 370. Recompute the ratios, which come out roughly as Kerala 1.74x, TN 1.94x, AP 1.30x, Gujarat 1.23x, Assam about 3.9x. 3) Recheck UP: US$2,650m (0.61x) does not reproduce from name/impagency/PDO matching, which gives about US$1,070m (0.26-0.29x). Either list the projects attributed to UP or correct the figure. 4) Drop '(YSRCP 2019-24)' as the AP qualifier. Most of AP's NDA-period commitment (Amaravati 2024, 24x7 Power 2017, Disaster Recovery 2015) was approved under the TDP government while it was an NDA ally, so AP is not an opposition counter-example. Describe it as 'mixed/allied'. 5) Note that TN's AIADMK was an NDA ally 2019-2023. 6) Kerala was UDF-run 2014-16 and LDF-run 2016-26; label it 'UDF/LDF (both non-NDA)'. 7) Add the aggregate alignment test (aligned-state share 57.8-58.0% vs 54.9% population-time share, 1.05-1.06x) as the strongest counter. 8) Correct the UPA control to HP about 9.0x and Odisha about 1.84x on the total-commitment basis, or show the file's own denominator. 9) Add the Jan Suraaj Bihar allegation (2025-11-16) as a related alleged item, and state that DEA was not asked.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: World Bank (IBRD/IDA) lent Government of India US$2.75bn of emergency money, April to July 2020. The dates hold. P173836, the US$1bn health loan, was approved on 2020-04-02 and signed 2020-04-03. P173943, the social protection loan, was approved 2020-05-14 and signed 2020-05-15. P174292, the MSME loan, was approved 2020-06-30 and signed 2020-07-06. Sitharaman was Finance Minister from 2019-05-31, so her tenure covers all three. The breakdown in strongestCase does not hold. It counts social protection as US$1.15bn, which adds P174027 (US$400m IDA). P174027 was approved 2020-12-15, about eight months after the health loan, so it falls outside the "within three months" window. The three figures also add to US$2.9bn, not US$2.75bn. The US$2.75bn is the Bank's headline commitment total: health 1bn + social protection "1bn" + MSME 0.75bn. The press release says the social protection 1bn was split into "an immediate allocation of $750 million for fiscal year 2020 and a $250 million second tranche that will be made available for fiscal year 2021".
verdicts.identityTest: The project IDs, borrower (Republic of India through DEA/MoF) and implementing agencies match the documents. But the claim treats all three operations as the same instrument, and they are not. P173836 is the "India COVID-19 Emergency Response and Health Systems Preparedness Project". It is an investment project with MoHFW as implementing agency, closed 2023-03-31, and it was paid out in instalments. Only P173943 and P174292, plus P174027 later, are development policy (budget support) operations, each single-tranche with proceeds credited to the Consolidated Fund. So "US$2.75bn single-tranche budget support" names the wrong instrument for US$1bn of the money. It is also wrong for the social protection commitment, which the Bank itself says was "funded in two phases".
verdicts.baseRate: Being a large borrower whose public debt is mostly held at home is not what separates India here: that is true of India, but not of most COVID-era World Bank borrowers. On the World Bank's own figures in the file, the 2020 budget-support money (US$1.5bn signed April to July, US$1.9bn with P174027) was about 0.05–0.07% of GDP. The ICR puts FY21 central government borrowing at a 9.5%-of-GDP deficit, "limited external financing needs". In the PD financing table, net external financing of the Union deficit is 0.0 in every year. A debt-trap story would need the Bank's service costs to be a binding constraint, and the record contains nothing showing that. Symmetry control: the Union's 2009–10 crisis borrowing under UPA was of similar size (about US$4bn+, including bank-recapitalisation and IIFCL operations), and the same lens reads it the same way. The finding does not depend on which party governed.
verdicts.denialFound: The government, the party concerned, gave its own account. Anurag Singh Thakur, then Minister of State for Finance, told the Rajya Sabha on 2020-09-15: "The World Bank has so far provided three loans worth $2.5 billion... The first loan relating to health measures worth $1,000 million was signed on 3rd April, 2020... As on date, $502.5 million has been disbursed" (reproduced at https://www.taxtmi.com/news?id=23143; the PIB/RS original was not opened). This contradicts both "US$2.75bn" as a 2020 signed amount and "single-tranche" for the health loan. On the other side, I found no named person or outlet claiming that the World Bank loans put India in a debt trap. The narrative has no stated proponent, so it risks debunking a claim nobody made.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was ordinary crisis lending of the kind the Bank gave more than 100 borrowers in 2020. Standard IBRD terms were 18.5 years with 5 years' grace; the IDA money was concessional. The loans part-financed domestic packages (PMGKY, ECLGS) that the government had already announced, at a cost below what India pays to borrow in the market. The prior actions all came before appraisal, and India's debt is overwhelmingly rupee-denominated and held by residents. The debunk verdict is correct in substance.
verdicts.reason: The debunk conclusion (no debt trap) survives. The primary sources confirm it. PD P174292 says "India's public debt is believed to remain sustainable because it is mostly denominated in domestic currency, of long/medium-term maturity, and predominantly held by residents". PD P173943 says the same. The press release gives IBRD terms of "a final maturity of 18.5 years including a grace period of five years", and the ICR gives the 9.5%-of-GDP FY21 deficit and "limited external financing needs". But the claim as written rests on a false factual premise. "US$2.75bn single-tranche budget support" is wrong on three counts. (a) US$1bn of it is the P173836 health investment project, which had paid out only US$502.5m by September 2020 according to the MoS Finance answer. (b) The social protection US$1bn was committed in two phases (750m + 250m, later 400m). (c) The components in strongestCase add to US$2.9bn, not 2.75bn, and include a December 2020 operation inside a "three months" window. The strongestCounter sentence "All three were single-tranche budget support" is therefore untrue. The external-debt figure is cited to our own fleet SPEC rather than to RBI. And no proponent of the debt-trap claim is identified. So the narrative must be corrected before publication. The verdict itself is our inference from documented facts, which makes it analytic.
verdicts.corrections: 1) strongestCase: replace with "US$2.75bn of emergency commitments were announced 2020-04-02 to 2020-06-30: health IPF P173836 US$1bn (IBRD), social protection DPF P173943 US$1bn headline (US$750m = IBRD 200 + IDA 550 committed; US$250m deferred to FY21), MSME DPL P174292 US$750m (IBRD). Signed by July 2020: US$2.5bn (MoS Finance, RS 2020-09-15). P174027 (US$400m IDA, 2020-12-15) followed; social protection total paid out US$1.151bn per ICR." 2) strongestCounter: replace "All three were single-tranche budget support" with "The two DPFs (and later P174027) were single-tranche budget support credited to the Consolidated Fund; the health loan was an investment project paid out in instalments (US$502.5m by Sept 2020). IBRD terms: 18.5-year final maturity, 5-year grace; IDA credits concessional." Keep the PD quote verbatim, and attribute the 9.5% FY21 deficit and "limited external financing needs" to the ICR. 3) Replace "~US$716bn in 2024 per fleet SPEC" with the RBI quarterly external-debt release figure and URL. Add the sovereign multilateral debt share from the Ministry of Finance "India's External Debt" status report. 4) Add a proponent field: no named source found making the debt-trap claim; mark it as a constructed/strawman narrative, or cite whoever made it. 5) Add a srcs entry for the Rajya Sabha answer of 2020-09-15 (PIB original) and for the 2020-04-02 press release (https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2020/04/02/world-bank-fast-tracks-1-billion-covid-19-support-for-india). 6) The press-release label says "2020-05-14" while the URL path is 2020/05/13; keep the content date 2020-05-14 but note the discrepancy. 7) Keep status "debunked", but mark the verdict as analytic (our inference from documented PD/ICR statements) with the innocentReading above.

verdicts.dateTest: Pass. Restated as: the World Bank (IBRD-85590, P153251) financed and verified SBM-G results through DLIs, Dec 2015 to Sep 30 2021, and IEG reviewed this in ICRR0023495 (Sep 2023). The source gives "approved in December 2015 and became effective in April 2016... actual closing date was September 30, 2021". It lists four Level 2 restructurings, dated Jul 1 2020, Jan 28 2021, Apr 12 2021 and Jun 30 2021. Every event falls inside the loan window, and the document ID 0990915231... matches the 2023-09-15 date.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The IEG ICR Review ICRR0023495 covers "Swachh Bharat Mission Support Operation (P153251)", loan IBRD-85590. The implementing agency is MDWS, and the programme is SBM-Gramin (rural) only, not SBM-Urban. The claim says "Swachh Bharat's ODF claims" without the rural limit, so it should say SBM-G.
verdicts.baseRate: A Satisfactory IEG outcome does not set this operation apart. Most IBRD operations get Moderately Satisfactory or better from IEG. Level 2 restructurings to extend closing dates or cancel undisbursed balances are routine in PforRs. Partial disbursement of INR-budgeted PforRs because of exchange-rate movements is common too. So "Satisfactory", "four restructurings" and "US$241m undisbursed" cannot count as evidence against the verification. Symmetry: the finance SPEC control (UPA 2004–14 against NDA 2014–26 borrowing) has no World Bank DLI-verified sanitation PforR from the UPA era to compare. Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan and the Total Sanitation Campaign were not financed this way, so no like-for-like reading exists.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and nobody was asked. There is no statement from the World Bank or MDWS on the specific framing "verified DLIs, not ODF declarations". Related material that disputes the ODF claims: Down To Earth, "Findings of annual rural sanitation survey questionable" (https://www.downtoearth.org.in/waste/findings-of-annual-rural-sanitation-survey-questionable-63472). It notes NARSS was government-backed and sampled about 92,000 households, against about 601,509 in NFHS. MDWS's official response to Reuters in 2019 defended the ODF figures: https://www.ibgnews.com/2019/05/17/official-response-from-mdws-to-recent-reuters-story-about-the-swachh-bharat-mission/
verdicts.innocentReading: This is a standard PforR. Money was paid out against DLIs, and a third-party Independent Verification Agency (IPE Global and Kantar, under NARSS) checked the DLI results against sample criteria. For DLI-2, a village counted as ODF if all households sustained toilet use, toilets were functional, and there were no visible faeces. All DLI targets were exceeded. IEG says the US$241m shortfall came from INR/USD exchange-rate savings: "only 84 percent of the original program financing was disbursed. This was due to savings resulting from exchange rate differences between the INR and the USD." The restructurings were Level 2 extensions and cancellations of about 8 months in total, with "No changes... to the Program scope and the PDO". None of this shows weak verification.
verdicts.reason:
The decisive problem is that the claim misquotes the efficacy rating. IEG did not rate overall efficacy "Substantial with shortcomings". It rated Objective 1, reducing open defecation (the ODF-relevant objective), as "High". It rated only Objective 2, MDWS capacity, as "Substantial with some shortcomings", and overall efficacy as "Substantial". The source says: "the efficacy of Objective 1 ... is rated High and the efficacy of Objective 2 ... is rated Substantial with some shortcomings... the ICRR rates the overall efficacy as Substantial." The claim uses the Objective 2 shortfall as a counter to the ODF verification. On ODF itself, the source says the reverse.

The claim also presents the US$1,259m of US$1,500m and the four restructurings as signs of weakness. The same source says all DLI targets were exceeded and that the shortfall was exchange-rate savings.

The core distinction holds only in part. DLI-2 did verify village ODF status, but through NARSS sample surveys by a contracted IVA, not by checking the Government's national ODF declarations. The source never states the "not of ODF declarations" point; it is our inference, which makes it analytic.

The real counter-evidence sits in the source but is left out. IEG rates Risk to Development Outcome High and says "Since 2018-2019, regular toilet use decreased by 13 percent on average in rural India." NARSS also ran only 3 of 5 planned rounds, with the first 20 months late.
verdicts.corrections:
1. tier: "contested" is not a contract tier. Use "analytic", with the IEG figures cited as documented sub-facts and an innocentReading attached.
2. text: replace "efficacy 'Substantial with shortcomings'" with "IEG: outcome Satisfactory; efficacy of the open-defecation objective High, MDWS-capacity objective 'Substantial with some shortcomings', overall Substantial".
3. strongestCounter: remove "IEG rated efficacy 'Substantial with some shortcomings'" (a misattribution). Replace it with the High sustainability risk: "Since 2018-2019, regular toilet use decreased by 13 percent on average in rural India." Add that NARSS ran 3 of 5 rounds and the first started 20 months late.
4. Reframe the US$241m undisbursed: add IEG's own reason ("savings resulting from exchange rate differences between the INR and the USD") and that "achievements of all DLIs exceeded targets". Note that the restructurings were Level 2 with no change to scope or PDO.
5. Restate "not of ODF declarations" as: DLI-2 verified village ODF status against NARSS sample criteria through a contracted IVA (IPE Global/Kantar); it did not audit the Government's national 100%-ODF declaration. Mark this as analytic inference, not source text.
6. Change "Swachh Bharat" to "SBM-Gramin (rural)". Add the Down To Earth critique of NARSS as a contrary source.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, restated as actor-did-thing-when: IBRD committed US$2,294m to Assam-attributed operations between 2014-05-26 and 2026-09-26, including the Assam Resilient Rural Bridges Program (P178581), approved 2024-03-01. The approval date checks out: board approval is 2024-03-01T00:00:00Z in both the v2 and v3 API, the PAD is dated 2024-02-07, and Loan Agreement 9632-IN was signed around 2024-09-18. A minor inconsistency: worldbank-projects.json quotes a PDO saying "approved on March 2, 2024". The period windows are applied consistently. Every NDA-period Assam approval falls on or after 2017-05-26. Assam was Congress-run from 2014 to May 2016 and had no approvals in that time; its only 2015 project (P128421) was dropped. Concentration in time: US$680m of the claimed US$2,294m (30%) was approved on a single day, 2026-01-13 (P511844 US$80m, P510002 US$350m, P507865 US$250m), shortly before the 2026 Assam assembly election. The bridges loan was approved just before the 2024 general election. This is timing only and proves nothing on its own. The UPA-period Assam total of US$524m (P084792 154 + P129686 50 + P096018 320) reproduces exactly.
verdicts.identityTest: The source node fin:ibrd is correct. Every NDA-period Assam operation is IBRD-only, and the bridges operation is IBRD Loan 9632-IN. The target energy:state-assam is the implementing entity (Public Works Roads Department, Government of Assam), not the borrower. The borrower is "India", which is how the Bank lends to all states under Article 293, so the edge should say "attributed to" rather than "receives". The Census population figure checks out: census2011.co.in gives Assam 31,205,576, which is 2.66% of the 1,175m population of the 25 attributed states. I independently reproduced 25 states, 1,175m population and 188 Active/Closed NDA projects worth US$49,796m. AMOUNT FAILS: the claim gives US$922m for P178581, taken from the v3 API field curr_ibrd_commitment. The Bank's own primary documents give US$452m. PAD5159 (2024-02-07) says: "PROGRAM APPRAISAL DOCUMENT ON A PROPOSED LOAN IN THE AMOUNT OF US$452 MILLION TO INDIA FOR AN ASSAM RESILIENT RURAL BRIDGES PROGRAM". The financing table reads "Total Operation Cost 564.71 … IBRD 452.00". Loan Agreement 9632-IN says: "The Bank agrees to lend to the Borrower the amount of four hundred and fifty two million Dollars ($452,000,000)". The v2 API also gives totalcommamt 452,000,000 and ibrdcommamt 452,000,000. I found no additional-financing operation or document for P178581; the latest document in the Bank's documents search is a 2025-02-13 procurement plan. The v3 figure of US$922m is larger than the whole operation's cost (US$565m in the PAD; lendprojectcost US$587m in the API), which is impossible for a real commitment. It is a v3 data artefact.
verdicts.baseRate: 11 of the 25 attributed states are above a 1.5x ratio under NDA (44%), so the property does single states out. However, 7 of those 11 are small hill or north-eastern states, and 3 are southern states run by opposition parties: Kerala 1.9x, Tamil Nadu 1.75x, Andhra Pradesh 1.6x. With the corrected US$452m bridges figure, Assam is at about 2.7x. That is still the highest ratio among states with more than 10m people, so a smaller but real deviation survives. The same lens shows higher outliers under UPA (Himachal Pradesh 9.7x, Uttarakhand 4.8x, Karnataka 2.1x). Assam's own UPA-period ratio recomputes to 1.67x on the unrounded 2.66% share (the file rounds it to 1.63). If the three projects approved on 2026-01-13 are removed, the corrected NDA ratio falls to about 1.75x, close to Assam's UPA level. The result depends on one board date. One more caution: across the portfolio, v3's current commitments differ from v2's original commitments in both directions (P165488 980 vs 460; P144447 1,856 vs 1,006; P102771 195 vs 1,195). The whole share calculation therefore depends on which field is used, and this was not stated.
verdicts.denialFound: none found; nobody was asked. This is an analytic ratio, and no party was put to it. The web search budget was exhausted, so I could not look for press responses. The Bank's own stated rationale is in PAD5159: the loan co-finances the state's "Assam State Bridge Infrastructure Program … approximately INR 11,165 Crore (US$1.34 billion, at US$1 = INR 83.34)", and it sits in a Series of Projects (SOP 1 is the bridges program, SOP 2 is the hill roads project P180672, later P510002). https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099022024175141268/text/BOSIB11f8ab45905c183f01859646519258.txt
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring explanation fits. Assam is a low-income, flood-exposed Brahmaputra state. The Bank finances part of a state-originated bridge program (about US$1.34bn in total), and it planned its Assam transport lending as a Series of Projects: bridges in 2024, then hill roads, where P180672 was dropped and re-approved as P510002 in 2026. This multi-year transport and disaster-resilience pipeline accounts for most of the total. The file's standard innocent reading, that small states have mechanically high per-capita ratios, fits Assam poorly: at 31m people it is the 14th most populous state. The better innocent explanations are the planned series and the fact that 30% of the total rests on a single board date. Opposition-run Kerala (1.9x) and Tamil Nadu (1.75x) show the same above-parity pattern. The ratio uses commitments, not disbursements, and attribution was done by regex on project names and agencies.
verdicts.reason: The claim's own headline component fails the source check. P178581 is a US$452m IBRD loan according to the Bank's PAD (PAD5159), Loan Agreement 9632-IN and the v2 API. The US$922m figure comes from a v3 API field and exceeds the operation's total cost of US$565m. Correcting it lowers Assam's NDA-period total from US$2,294m to US$1,824m, its share from 8.9% to 7.2% (on a denominator of US$25,284m), and its ratio from 3.3x to about 2.7x. So the stated amount, share and ratio are all wrong as written. A smaller deviation, about 2.7x against about 1.7x under UPA, does survive as an analytic observation. It is heavily concentrated on the three approvals of 2026-01-13, and without them the ratio is about 1.75x.
verdicts.corrections: worldbank:c056. Text/lab: replace "3.3x … (US$2,294m, 8.9%) vs 1.6x under UPA; Assam Resilient Rural Bridges US$922m" with "≈2.7x … (US$1,824m, 7.2%) vs 1.7x under UPA; Assam Resilient Rural Bridges US$452m (IBRD Loan 9632-IN)". d: NDA state-attributed denominator US$25,284m (not 25,754), and state which field was used (curr_total_commitment, with P178581 overridden by the PAD figure). Add to d: "US$680m (37% of the corrected total) approved on 2026-01-13 in three operations; excluding that date the ratio is ≈1.75x." srcs: add PAD5159 https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099022024175141268/text/BOSIB11f8ab45905c183f01859646519258.txt and Loan Agreement 9632-IN https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099091824085528427/text/P17858113506d00921a826172bccbf5c6c8.txt. Wording: "receives" becomes "has attributed to it"; the borrower is India. innocentReading: add the bridges and hill-roads Series of Projects and the state's own INR 11,165 cr bridge program, and drop the small-state framing for Assam. Propagate the fix to: worldbank.json entity energy:state-assam (publicRole "3.3x" and the d line "US$922m"); the topLoansSince2000 entry for P178581 (usdm 922 to 452); the narrative strongestCase "Assam … 3.3x" to ≈2.7x; the symmetryCheck "Assam 3.3x"; and worldbank-projects.json worldbank:c0795 (a 7714.31 cr to about 3,782 cr at ₹83.67, or 3,767 cr at the PAD rate of ₹83.34; d "US$922 m" to "US$452 m"). Check the other large v3/v2 discrepancies (P165488, P144447, P507508, P507910) before reusing v3 curr_total_commitment elsewhere.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: IBRD (actor) committed a larger share of state-attributed lending to Gujarat (thing) under NDA, 2014-05-26 to 2026-09-26, than under UPA, 2004-05-22 to 2014-05-25 (when). I re-fetched both API pages (1,117 projects). The UPA-period Gujarat figure is one project, P114827 GSHP-II, US$175m, board-approved 2013-12-13, which falls inside the UPA window. The NDA-period projects are P173704 GOAL (2021-03-24), P177915 GOAL-AF (2022-06-21), P178252 SRESTHA-G (2022-09-21) and P175728 Ahmedabad (2022-11-22). All four are in the NDA window. Timing needs a caveat. All of Gujarat's NDA-period state-attributed lending was approved in 2021-22, seven or more years after the change of government. From 2014 to 2020 Gujarat got nothing state-attributed: only its part of the multi-state NCRMP-II (US$308m), and Gujarat Urban Development Program P094722 (US$180m, 2014-07) was dropped. The UPA-period number is also shaped by two Gujarat projects dropped before approval: Gujarat Urban Services P066441 (US$350m, 2005) and Gujarat Urban Reform P073161 (US$100m, 2007). The API does not say why they were dropped. The period assignment is correct. The finding that Gujarat's share went from low to high holds for board-approval dates.
verdicts.identityTest: The node energy:govt-of-gujarat is the Government of Gujarat, which the file already uses as the GOAL borrower-state. That match is fine. The subject fin:ibrd is correct: every project counted has an IBRD commitment and no IDA. The amount is wrong. The API field curr_total_commitment for P173704 is 750,000,000, but curr_ibrd_commitment and totalamt are 500,000,000, and grantamt is 250,000,000. The file's own claim worldbank:c006 (from the PAD) gives GOAL as US$500m IBRD, Loan 9219-IN. The claim's Gujarat NDA total of US$1,630m = 750 + 250 (AF) + 350 + 280. So it counts a US$250m that is not IBRD money on top of GOAL's US$500m. That extra US$250m is either the Additional Financing counted twice or co-financing inside the parent project's total. Gujarat's correct IBRD figure is 500 + 250 + 350 + 280 = US$1,380m.
verdicts.baseRate: The file's own base rate says 11 of 25 states had a loan-share/population-share ratio above 1.5 in the NDA period. Gujarat's 1.24 (about 1.14 once corrected) is below that threshold, so its NDA level does not stand out. Only the change between periods is distinctive, and the file's symmetry check finds the lens gives dispersed, 'alarming-looking' ratios in both periods and for both blocs. Odisha and Karnataka fell, Gujarat rose, and small hill and north-eastern states dominate the extremes. Gujarat's history before UPA also matters. In 2000-02 it received about US$824m (GSHP-I US$381m, Earthquake Reconstruction US$443m), under NDA-I, and this came from need (the 2001 earthquake) and the project cycle. It shows Gujarat's share moves with that cycle, not just with who holds the Union government.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Nobody was asked: not DEA, the World Bank or the Government of Gujarat. That is appropriate for an analytic ratio. The record's upgradeIf, which asks for a DEA allocation note or CAG/CPF text, is the right route.
verdicts.innocentReading: The record's own innocent reading applies. States borrow through DEA under Article 293. The state pipeline and FRBM borrowing headroom determine uptake. There is a multi-year lag between preparation and board approval. Here the lag cuts against a simple political reading, since Gujarat's NDA-era approvals only came in 2021-22. In the UPA years Gujarat's pipeline existed but was dropped (Urban Services US$350m in 2005, Urban Reform US$100m in 2007). That fits the state choosing not to borrow, or the projects failing preparation, just as well as it fits the Union excluding the state. Attribution by name regex leaves out multi-state projects in both periods (ICZM 2010, which included Gujarat; NCRMP-II 2015).
verdicts.reason: The claim fails as written on the amount. It says GOAL was US$750m. The API's IBRD field and the PAD (the file's own worldbank:c006) both give US$500m. The US$750m is the API's curr_total_commitment, which includes US$250m of non-IBRD or additional-financing money. Adding the separate GOAL-AF US$250m on top counts US$250m twice or wrongly, which inflates Gujarat's NDA total from US$1,380m to US$1,630m. The same curr_total_commitment problem inflates the state-attributed denominator: projects where total exceeds IBRD+IDA include Amaravati 1600/800, Kerala 370/125, Chennai 300/150, Punjab 210/105 and WB irrigation 290/145. By my rough re-estimate the corrected NDA ratio is about 1.14, not 1.24; that figure needs a full recompute. The direction (a low UPA-era share rising to above population share under NDA) survives, and the analytic tier with an innocentReading is the right tier once the numbers are fixed. The UPA figures (US$175m, 1.5%, 0.29x) check out against the API.
verdicts.corrections: text: replace 'GOAL US$750m' with 'GOAL US$500m + GOAL-AF US$250m'. d: Gujarat NDA commitment US$1,630m -> US$1,380m (IBRD). Recompute every state numerator and the US$25,754m NDA denominator (and the US$11,799m UPA denominator) using curr_ibrd_commitment + curr_ida_commitment, not curr_total_commitment, because the total field includes co-financing/AF (e.g. P173704 total 750 vs IBRD 500; P507508 1600 vs 800; P174778 370 vs 125). Restate the ratio (estimated at about 1.14, to be confirmed by recompute). Add to d/innocentReading: Gujarat had no state-attributed approvals in 2014-2020 (all NDA-period Gujarat lending was approved 2021-22); UPA-period Gujarat projects P066441 (US$350m) and P073161 (US$100m) were dropped, reason unknown from the API; in 2000-02 Gujarat got about US$824m under NDA-I. Keep tier analytic and pred analytic. No family, religion or ethnicity framing is involved.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: IBRD/IDA commitments to AP rose from 0.35x population share under UPA (2004-05-22 to 2014-05-25) to 1.62x under NDA (2014-05-26 to 2026-09-26). Approval dates are in the right windows. P507508 Amaravati Integrated Urban Development Program: boardapprovaldate 2024-12-19, which is correct and falls under the TDP-led NDA-ally government (June 2024 on). The statement that the rise spans TDP, YSRCP and TDP-NDA governments misstates the politics. TDP was an NDA ally from 2014 to March 2018, and P155038 AP 24x7 Power (US$400m, 2017-05-26) was approved while it was an ally. The earlier Amaravati project, P159808 (US$300m IBRD), was Dropped in 2019 under YSRCP. So the largest single item exists only because of the 2024 NDA-ally government. It is not evidence of continuity across opposition governments.
verdicts.identityTest: Failed on the node's scope. The population denominator is undivided AP (Census 2011, 7.2%), and the NDA numerator includes a Telangana project (P143608, US$75m). The UPA numerator, however, leaves out every undivided-AP project that the API now labels 'Andhra Pradesh and Telangana' or that names both states' agencies. Those are P100789 (US$189m, 2007), P101650 (US$150m, 2009), P096021 (US$320m, 2009), P071250 (US$300m, 2009) and P100954 (US$450.6m, 2010), about US$1,410m in total. They were single-state loans to undivided AP, relabelled after the 2014 bifurcation, and the regex put them in the 'US$1.4bn multi-state' bucket. The UPA figure of US$292m is exactly P075174 (225) + P104724 (65) + P122241 (1.9) = 291.9. Also, Amaravati's curr_total_commitment of US$1,600m includes co-financing. The API's own curr_ibrd_commitment for P507508 is 800,000,000, so the Bank's own loan is US$800m, not US$1,600m.
verdicts.baseRate: The record's own symmetryCheck says the per-capita lens is 'alarming' in both periods and for both blocs: 11 of 25 states are above 1.5x under NDA, and dispersion is similar under UPA. Once the UPA undivided-AP loans are restored, AP comes to about US$1,701m out of about US$13,209m state-attributed, a 12.9% share against 7.2% of population, or about 1.79x under UPA. That is above the NDA figure of 1.62x. If only the Bank's own IBRD share of Amaravati (US$800m) is counted, the NDA ratio falls further, to roughly 1.1-1.2x. The 'rise' becomes a flat or falling ratio. AP was above parity under both UPA and NDA, so the property does not discriminate.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable: this is an analytic comparison and no wrongdoing is alleged. None found; the parties were not asked (DEA, the AP Finance Department and the World Bank India office).
verdicts.innocentReading: Undivided AP was one of the Bank's main state partners under UPA: the 2004-10 economic reform loans, roads, municipal, water sector, tanks and RWSS projects. After 2014 the API relabelled those projects as AP-and-Telangana, and the attribution regex reclassified them as multi-state. That created an artificially low UPA baseline. The post-2014 figure is dominated by one 2024 co-financed Amaravati programme (US$800m WB + ADB) that restarts a 2016-19 pipeline. That is timing, not a change of regime.
verdicts.reason: This is a methodological artefact. The UPA baseline of 0.35x (US$292m) leaves out about US$1.41bn of World Bank loans to undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2007-2010 (P100789, P101650, P096021, P071250, P100954). The same API relabels them 'Andhra Pradesh and Telangana', and the regex binned them as multi-state. Yet the NDA numerator includes Telangana and the population denominator is undivided AP. Corrected, UPA is about 1.79x, which is at or above the NDA 1.62x, so the headline 'rise' disappears. Separately, the US$1,600m Amaravati figure is the programme total. The API gives curr_ibrd_commitment as US$800m for P507508.
verdicts.corrections: Kill c058 as stated. If it is rebuilt: (1) Reattribute P100789, P101650, P096021, P071250 and P100954 (US$1,409.6m) to AP for 2004-14, with the same recomputation for any other bifurcated state, and recompute all state ratios, since the UPA denominator changes for every state including c057 Gujarat and c059 Kerala. (2) Amaravati P507508: use US$800m curr_ibrd_commitment as the World Bank amount and note that US$1,600m is the programme total including co-financing, or use curr_ibrd+curr_ida throughout. (3) Fix the political framing: TDP was an NDA ally from 2014 to March 2018. Say that the 2016-19 Amaravati loan P159808 was dropped in 2019, not that the rise 'spans opposition governments'. (4) Either split the node into AP-residual plus Telangana for NDA with post-2014 population, or keep undivided-AP scope consistently in both periods. (5) Also fix the text field: the predicate text 'rose from 0.35x to 1.62x' has to go.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: World Bank (IBRD+IDA) approved single-state commitments to Kerala of US$1,395m between 2014-05-26 and 2026-09-26 (NDA) and US$571m between 2004-05-22 and 2014-05-25 (UPA), while Kerala was opposition-run in both periods. I re-fetched both API pages (1,117 projects) and the period totals match the claim: UPA 177 projects / US$37,496m and NDA 188 / US$49,796m. For the NDA period Kerala was opposition-run throughout: UDF under a Congress CM 2014–16, then LDF 2016 onward. For the UPA period it was not. The UPA-period Kerala money is P102624 (2011-03-29, US$200m, LDF government, when the CPI(M) had been in opposition since July 2008), P121774 (2011-12-15, US$155.3m) and P130339 (2013-05-14, US$216m). The last two were approved under Oommen Chandy's Congress-led UDF government (from 2011-05-18), and Congress was the UPA's own lead party. So US$371m of the US$571m (65%) was approved while Kerala was ruled by the Union's lead party. "Opposition-run in both periods" fails the date test for the UPA half of the claim.
verdicts.identityTest:
1. Wrong subject node. The subject is fin:ibrd, but the Kerala money is not all IBRD. P169907 (US$250m) is an IDA credit.
2. The numerator includes non-Bank money. The US$1,395m is the sum of curr_total_commitment over P169907 (250), P168633 (144.96), P174778 (370), P177980 (150), P178254 (200) and P503872 (280). For two of these, curr_total_commitment is larger than the Bank's own commitment:
   - P174778: API curr_ibrd_commitment/totalamt is 125,000,000, with grantamt 245,000,000.
   - P168633: IBRD 72,560,000, with grantamt 72,400,000.
   Counting IBRD+IDA only, Kerala's NDA-period total is US$1,078m, not US$1,395m.
3. When I recompute with a name/impagency regex, Bank-only money puts Kerala at about 1.74x, against 2.04x on curr_total_commitment in the same run. The claim's own denominator of US$25,754m is not reproducible from the file, because the attribution regex is not published.
4. The UPA figure (US$571m, 1.71x) holds on both measures, because none of those projects is co-financed.
5. The population side is fine: Kerala's Census 2011 population of 33.4m out of 1,175m for the 25 states gives 2.84%.
verdicts.baseRate: Being above parity does not single Kerala out. By the file's own claim c063, 11 of 25 states are above 1.5x under NDA. The northeastern and hill states are high whichever party runs them, and three southern opposition-run states are above 1.5x. Under UPA, my regex puts Kerala at about 1.9x, alongside Tamil Nadu (2.3x), Karnataka (2.4x), Assam (1.9x) and Punjab (1.7x).
verdicts.denialFound: No denial applies, since nobody is accused of anything. No one was asked. Neither the World Bank nor DEA (the Finance Ministry's Department of Economic Affairs) was asked how states are selected, and none of the documents opened gives a DEA note or CPF text on state selection.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Kerala pipeline is driven by the 2018 floods. The Resilient Kerala DPO, the PforR and its additional financing make up US$770m of the NDA-period Bank-plus-co-finance figure. On top of that, Kerala has a long record as a borrower, having been above parity under Congress-run UDF governments during UPA, and it has the capacity to prepare projects. The corrected facts support the claim's own innocent reading more strongly: Kerala sits above parity whether it is aligned with the Union (UDF under UPA) or in opposition (LDF/UDF under NDA).
verdicts.reason:
The ratios reproduce from the Projects API, but the claim as written fails on two counts.
1. The framing is wrong. The label says Kerala is "an opposition-run state above parity in both periods". Under UPA, 65% of Kerala's commitments (P121774 and P130339, US$371m) were approved while a Congress-led UDF government ran Kerala, and Congress led the UPA. The UPA-period comparison is therefore an aligned-state case, not an opposition-state case.
2. The 1.9x NDA figure is inflated. It counts about US$317m of co-financing (P174778 grantamt 245m, P168633 grantamt 72.4m) as World Bank commitments under an "fin:ibrd" subject. On IBRD+IDA money alone, Kerala is at about 1.7x.
Kerala does remain above parity in both periods, so the claim should stay analytic with corrected text, not be killed.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Change lab to: "Kerala ~1.7–1.9x its population share under NDA (1.7x under UPA): above parity under both opposition (2014–26) and Union-aligned UDF (2011–14) governments."
2. Change s from fin:ibrd to a World Bank IBRD+IDA node (for example fin:world-bank or fin:wbg). P169907 is IDA.
3. In d, state that US$1,395m uses curr_total_commitment and includes co-financing on P174778 (IBRD 125m of 370m) and P168633 (IBRD 72.56m of 144.96m). Also give the Bank-only figure: US$1,078m, about 1.7x on a consistently recomputed denominator.
4. In d, split the UPA figure by government: US$200m under the LDF (P102624, 2011-03) and US$371m under the Congress-led UDF (P121774, P130339).
5. Publish the state-attribution regex, or the per-project attribution list, so the US$25,754m and US$11,799m denominators can be reproduced.
6. Add a UPA-alignment control to symmetryCheck: Kerala, Tamil Nadu (DMK, a UPA ally to 2013) and others were above parity while aligned with the Union.
7. Keep tier as analytic.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: the World Bank approved state-attributed commitments to Tamil Nadu equal to 1.75x its population share from 2014-05-26 to 2026-09-26 and 2.08x from 2004-05-22 to 2014-05-25, "consistently above parity under DMK and AIADMK governments". I split the file's own project set by TN government, using approval dates from the API and the file's rule of excluding multi-state projects: AIADMK 2004-05 to May 2006 got US$685m. DMK May 2006 to May 2011 got US$807m. AIADMK May 2011 to May 2014 got only US$2.8m (P129119, a TA grant), because the file's UPA total of US$1,495m excludes P143382, the US$236m TN and Puducherry Coastal Disaster Risk Reduction project. Against about US$3.1bn of state-attributed approvals in that window, that is roughly 0.01x, far below parity. AIADMK May 2014 to May 2021 got US$1,648m (about 2.4x on my crude denominator). DMK May 2021 to 2026 got US$1,102m (about 1.35x). So "consistently above parity under DMK and AIADMK governments" is false for AIADMK 2011-14 under the file's own method. The record's from field (2014-05-26) also leaves out the UPA window the claim cites. Approval date also trails the government that prepared the project by 2 to 4 years, which the file itself says.

Of the UPA-period TN US$1,495m, about US$807m is IDA: P075058 US$110.83m, P079708 US$274m, P090768 US$150m of its US$485m, P118830 US$117.7m and P107668 US$154m. The TN entity (Government of Tamil Nadu and its agencies named in impagency) matches the source.

The file's own symmetryCheck says the per-capita lens gives similar dispersion in both periods and for both political blocs, driven by small states and pipeline timing. TN is also a high-capacity, repeat borrower since the 1970s: 16 or more TN-named operations before 2004 appear in the API. Being above parity is its long-run norm, not something tied to a particular regime.
