verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is "IBRD/IDA approved US$2,650m for Uttar Pradesh in 2014-05-26..2026-09-26 and US$1,637m in 2004-05-22..2014-05-25, and UP is the largest BJP-run state in both periods". UP's governments were: SP (Mulayam Singh Yadav, 2003-08 to 2007-05), BSP (Mayawati, 2007-05 to 2012-03), SP (Akhilesh Yadav, 2012-03 to 2017-03-19) and BJP (Yogi Adityanath, 2017-03-19 onward). So UP was not BJP-run at any point in the UPA window, and it was SP-run for about the first 2.8 years of the NDA window. The label "the largest BJP-run state is below parity in both periods" projects post-2017 party control back onto 2004-2017. The date test fails for the UPA half of the label and partly fails for the NDA half. One more detail: every UP-named approval in the NDA window is dated 2017-12-20 or later, so none falls in the SP years 2014-17, although P147864 and P146936 were prepared under the SP government.
verdicts.identityTest: The node energy:state-uttar-pradesh (Government of UP) is the correct entity, but the dollar figures attached to it include national projects that are not UP's. I re-fetched both API pages (1,117 projects). The NDA figure of US$2,650m equals exactly 40 (P146936 UP Pro-Poor Tourism) + 400 (P147864 UP Core Road Network) + 325 (P178253 UP Agriculture Growth) + 305 (P510253 UP Clean Air) + 600 (P162849 "India Energy Efficiency Scale-up Program", borrower/impagency EESL, a central PSU) + 980 (P165488 "India Energy Efficiency Scale-Up Program Guarantee", no state named). The UPA figure of US$1,637m equals exactly 620 (P077856 Lucknow-Muzaffarpur NH, which crosses into Bihar) + 197 (P112033) + 152 (P100304) + 360 (P122770) + 307.13 (P119043 "India: Scaling Up Sustainable and Responsible Microfinance", SIDBI, national) + 1.1 (P119894 "Scaling Up Deployment of Renewable Energy Technology", national). The pattern points to a case-insensitive "UP" token matching "Scale-up" and "Scaling Up". A second possible cause is fetch-worldbank.mjs line 150, which gives fin:sidbi st:'up' because SIDBI's head office is in Lucknow. Either way, about US$1,580m (NDA) and US$308m (UPA) of national-programme money is attributed to UP. The entity's own `d` field lists only the three UP-named NDA projects (US$1,030m), which contradicts the US$2,650m in this claim.
verdicts.baseRate: Large, populous, low-income states sit below per-capita parity almost regardless of which party runs them. The file's own c063 puts six states below 0.6x under NDA: UP, Bihar (JD(U)/RJD), MP, Haryana, Odisha (BJD until 2024) and Chhattisgarh (Congress 2018-23). The 11 states above 1.5x are mainly small hill/north-eastern states (7 of 11). A state with a 17% population share being below parity is the expected result of the denominator, so it does not discriminate by party. There is also an internal inconsistency: c063 lists UP as "below 0.6" while c061 gives 0.61.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. This is an analytic comparison that accuses no party. None found; nobody asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: UP's low per-capita share reflects three things: its size (17% of population, so a few US$300-400m projects cannot reach parity), limited implementing capacity and project pipeline, and project preparation lag. Much Bank money that physically reaches UP arrives through central or multi-state vehicles: EDFC-I/II/III (DFCCIL), National Ganga River Basin I/II, EESL and SIDBI. State-name attribution cannot capture that money, so it neither counts toward UP nor proves any exclusion. The existing innocentReading already covers most of this and is adequate.
verdicts.reason: Both ratios rest on misattributed amounts. The API shows that US$1,580m of the NDA-period "UP" total is the two national EESL "Scale-up" operations (P162849, P165488). US$308m of the UPA-period total is the national SIDBI "Scaling Up" microfinance project and a US$1.1m "Scaling Up" renewables project. Only US$1,070m in the NDA window is UP-specific. On a corrected denominator (25,754 − 1,580 = 24,174), UP's NDA share is about 4.4% against a 17.0% population share, a ratio of about 0.26x, not 0.61x. UPA is about 1,329 / 11,491 = 11.6%, about 0.68x, or about 0.36x if the multi-state Lucknow-Muzaffarpur highway is excluded. The direction "below parity in both periods" survives and actually strengthens. The label's premise does not survive: "the largest BJP-run state … in both periods" is false chronologically, because UP was SP/BSP-run throughout 2004-2017. The claim as written is wrong on its figures and its framing. The underlying analytic observation can stay at the analytic tier once corrected, and the denominators for all 25 state ratios (c058-c063) should be recomputed after removing the "up" false positives.
verdicts.corrections: 1) lab → "Uttar Pradesh ≈0.26x (2014-26) and ≈0.68x (2004-14) of population share: below parity under SP/BSP governments (2004-17) and under BJP (2017-)". Drop "largest BJP-run state … in both periods", or say "BJP-run since 2017-03-19". 2) d → remove P162849 (US$600m, EESL) and P165488 (US$980m, EESL guarantee) from the NDA UP total, giving US$1,070m (P146936 40, P147864 400, P178253 325, P510253 305). Remove P119043 (US$307m, SIDBI) and P119894 (US$1.1m) from the UPA total, giving US$1,329m (flag P077856 Lucknow-Muzaffarpur US$620m as UP+Bihar multi-state). Recompute the state-attributed denominators (≈24,174 NDA and ≈11,491 UPA, pending a full recheck of the other states) and restate the ratios. 3) Fix the attribution code: match state codes only as whole tokens in agency/borrower fields, never in project_name ("Scale-up"/"Scaling Up"), and do not attribute SIDBI (HQ Lucknow) or EESL loans to a state by headquarters. 4) Update the entity energy:state-uttar-pradesh publicRole ("0.61x … largest BJP-run state") to match, and reconcile c063's "Below 0.6: UP" with c061. 5) Add to d the UP chief-minister windows: SP 2003-07, BSP 2007-12, SP 2012-17, BJP 2017-. 6) Keep tier analytic and keep the innocentReading. Add to killIf: "attribution recomputed from Bank PAD location data".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim restated: "World Bank board approvals attributed to Karnataka (and Odisha), as a share of all single-state commitments divided by Census-2011 population share, were 2.12x (and 2.03x) for 2004-05-22 to 2014-05-25 and 0.79x (and 0.39x) for 2014-05-26 to 2026-09-26." I checked every project's boardapprovaldate against these windows, and they sit correctly in their periods. Two limits: the NDA window is 12.3 years against 10 for UPA, although share-based ratios cancel the length difference; and early-NDA approvals (for example P149811 on 2014-06-25) were prepared under UPA. The claim names no officeholder, so there is no tenure to test.
verdicts.identityTest: Partly fails. (1) The source node is wrong. The edge uses s=fin:ibrd, but about half of the UPA-period money was IDA credit: Karnataka UPA is IBRD US$598m plus IDA US$574m, and Odisha UPA is IBRD US$469.5m plus IDA US$388.8m (SEDL I/II, Rural Livelihoods and Disaster Recovery were IDA or blended). A fin:ida node exists in the file. (2) Karnataka UPA wrongly includes P110371 Sustainable Urban Transport Project (US$105.23m). That is a national MoUD project, borrower DEA, with implementing agencies in Indore, Hubli-Dharwad, Mysore, Naya Raipur and Pimpri-Chinchwad. It matched only on 'Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation', so it is a multi-state project and the file's own rule should have excluded it. (3) Karnataka UPA also counts P119295 'KARNATAKA WIND' (US$13.59m) and P100352 (US$1.32m). Both show IBRD and IDA commitments of 0/None and are carbon-finance or trust-fund items, not loans. On the NDA side, P149811 (US$4.55m) is also non-IBRD/IDA. (4) The edge targets energy:state-karnataka, but the text also asserts Odisha's figures. The file has no Odisha entity, so the Odisha half of the claim sits on an edge that does not point at Odisha.
verdicts.baseRate: Large per-state swings between periods are common under this lens. From the same file: Gujarat went 0.29x to 1.24x, AP 0.35x to 1.62x, Assam 1.63x to 3.3x, HP 9.7x to 6.3x, and UP 0.82x to 0.61x. A shift of more than 0.5x in either direction is the norm across roughly 25 states, so Karnataka's and Odisha's falls are among the larger ones but not unusual in kind. Symmetry control (SPEC: BJP-run vs opposition-run states): Odisha was BJD-run for the whole period until 2024. Karnataka was Congress-run 2013–18 and 2023–, and BJP-run 2008–13 and 2019–23. The Karnataka fall covers both BJP and Congress years, and the lens gives no party-aligned reading, which matches the file's narrative status 'unsupported'.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and nobody was asked. The claim is an analytic ratio that accuses no one. Neither the Karnataka nor the Odisha government, nor DEA, has made a statement on the ratio that I could find.
verdicts.innocentReading: The innocent reading in the record holds and is strengthened by the data. (a) The multi-state exclusion hits both states hard in the NDA period. REWARD P172187 (US$102.8m) is a Karnataka–Odisha project. DRIP-AF P166977 and DRIP-II P170873 (US$137m plus US$419m) include both states. NCRMP-II P144726 (US$308m) includes Karnataka. Strengthening Coastal Resilience P180932 (US$212.6m) is Karnataka plus Tamil Nadu. Counting each state's share of these would raise both NDA ratios. (b) Odisha's UPA figure is inflated by one-off post-cyclone and budget-support credits (SEDL I/II US$350m, Disaster Recovery US$153m after Phailin, approved 2014-02-20). (c) Odisha's fiscal position improved after 2014, and its reduced appetite for external borrowing is a plausible borrower-side explanation. (d) Pipeline lag and FRBM ceilings apply.
verdicts.reason: I pulled both API pages (1,117 projects) and reproduced the arithmetic exactly using the file's own method. Karnataka UPA is US$1,292m and NDA US$1,044m (P149811 4.55 + P130544 100 + P176107 150 + P179039 363 + P506272 426). Odisha UPA is US$858m (125+225+82.35+196+76.94+153) and NDA US$364m (119+165+79.925). The ratios 2.12, 0.79, 2.03 and 0.39 all follow from the stated denominators. So the source supports the numbers as computed, and the direction of both falls survives. However, the Karnataka UPA figure includes a national multi-city project (SUTP, US$105m) and two non-loan carbon-finance items (US$14.9m). Dropping them gives about US$1,172m, or roughly 1.9x rather than 2.12x. The NDA side, after dropping the US$4.55m non-loan pilot, stays at about 0.78x. Odisha's figures are clean. Karnataka is overstated by about 0.2x and the lender node is wrong, but the substance (a large fall for both states, spanning BJP and non-BJP state governments) holds. The analytic tier is correct: this is our own ratio, it implies no wrongdoing, and it carries an innocentReading. It passes only with the corrections below.
verdicts.corrections: 1. lab/text: change 'Karnataka fell from 2.12x' to 'Karnataka fell from ~1.9x (2.12x before removing SUTP P110371 and carbon-finance items P119295/P100352)'. In d, restate Karnataka UPA as US$1,172m of IBRD/IDA commitments and recompute the UPA denominator (US$11,799m less about US$120m, affecting every c056–c063 UPA ratio slightly). Drop P149811 (US$4.55m, no IBRD/IDA) from Karnataka NDA, giving US$1,039m and 0.78x. 2. Attribution rule: filter to curr_ibrd_commitment + curr_ida_commitment > 0, and move P110371 into the multi-state bucket. 3. Lender: s=fin:ibrd is wrong for the IDA portions. Either use a World Bank group node, or split the claim into fin:ibrd and fin:ida edges; UPA Karnataka is about 51% IBRD and 49% IDA, and UPA Odisha about 55% IBRD and 45% IDA. 4. Split out Odisha: create an Odisha state entity (e.g. energy:state-odisha, st:'or') and a separate analytic edge for 2.03x→0.39x, so the Karnataka edge makes no claim about another state. 5. Add to innocentReading: 'the excluded multi-state projects REWARD (Karnataka+Odisha), DRIP-II, NCRMP-II and Coastal Resilience (Karnataka+TN) disproportionately involve these two states in the NDA period; Odisha's UPA total includes post-Phailin disaster credit and SEDL budget support'. 6. Add a symmetry note that Karnataka had BJP governments in 2008–13 and 2019–23, so its fall spans both parties.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated: "IBRD/IDA board approvals for India attributable to one state were 31% of commitments under UPA (2004-05-22 to 2014-05-25) and 52% under NDA (2014-05-26 to 2026-09-26)." The era windows are right. The shares, however, come from the Union-level era, while the party labels have to be tested against who ruled each state on each project's approval date. The claim never makes that join (fetch-worldbank.mjs:742 says "this file does not carry it, so no party share is asserted here"), and when it is made, several labels fail. (a) Chhattisgarh ("BJP-run"): all four NDA-era approvals (P166578 2019-02-21, P170645 and P170873 2020-12-15, P179249 2023-06-26) came under the Congress government of Dec 2018 to Dec 2023. (b) Andhra Pradesh ("southern opposition-run"): US$565m was approved in 2014-17 under the TDP while it was an NDA partner, and P507508 Amaravati (US$800m, 2024-12-19) was approved under TDP-NDA and follows the Union Budget 2024-25 promise of multilateral finance for Amaravati. About 69% of AP's NDA-era total was approved under an NDA-allied government. (c) Tamil Nadu: US$1,648m was approved under the AIADMK before May 2021, and the AIADMK was an NDA ally from 2019 to 2023, so the state is mixed. (d) Most of the hill and north-eastern states above 1.5x were governed by BJP or NDA/NEDA partners at the approval dates: Assam (every approval from 2017 onward), Uttarakhand (2017-24), Tripura 2023, Sikkim 2023, Meghalaya (2018 onward), Nagaland, and Mizoram in 2021. Only Kerala was opposition-run throughout.
verdicts.identityTest: The source node is wrong. The commitments are IBRD plus IDA combined, and IDA was large under UPA, so s=fin:ibrd misnames the lender. It should be a World Bank Group node, or the claim should be split by IBRD and IDA. The target node min:ministry-of-finance is acceptable as the formal borrower. The state attribution is the author's own regex, not a World Bank field. The pre-fetched state field also shows misattribution risk: P144726, the multi-state National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project II (US$308m), is tagged 'ga', which would put Goa, a BJP-run state, at about 10x if multi-state projects were not excluded. The claim does say it excludes US$1.4bn of multi-state projects. For the UPA era, AP's population denominator has to be undivided Andhra Pradesh (84.6m), not post-2014 AP (49.4m).
verdicts.baseRate: The pattern is non-discriminating by construction. Most of the states above 1.5x (8 of 11, not 7: Tripura is north-eastern and was miscounted) have under 1% of India's population each, so one project of US$100-300m pushes the ratio past 1.5x. Under UPA the same lens gives HP about 7x, Uttarakhand about 4x and Puducherry above 13x, so the shape is the same in both eras. The rise in state share is method-sensitive: recomputing from research/raw/finance/worldbank-projects.json (IBRD+IDA only, Dropped and pipeline projects excluded, pre-fetched state field) gives about 38% under UPA (US$13.6bn of US$36.0bn) and about 53% under NDA (US$23.6bn of US$44.9bn). The direction holds, but the UPA figure moves by 7 points depending on the attribution rule. Haryana comes out at 0.61x with P510686 (US$300m, 2025-12-10) included, which is borderline for "below 0.6x".
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. This is our own analytic comparison and accuses no party of anything, so no denial was sought or found (none found, not asked).
verdicts.innocentReading: Small states get high per-capita ratios mechanically. Projects take 2-4 years to prepare, so the pipeline lags any change of government. The Bank moved toward state-level operations and PforRs after 2014, and IDA graduation removed cheap central credits. State FRBM ceilings and implementing capacity limit borrowing. State external borrowing is routed through DEA under Article 293. Any of these explains both the rising state share and the scatter of ratios without reference to party. The stored innocentReading already says this and is adequate.
verdicts.reason: The headline shares (31% to 52%) survive only as a method-dependent analytic figure. The party half of the claim fails the date test. It says "no party pattern" and supports that with labels that are wrong at the approval dates. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are called "southern opposition-run", but most of AP's money (including the US$800m Amaravati programme) and most of TN's pre-2021 money was approved under NDA-allied governments. Chhattisgarh is called "BJP-run" below 0.6x, but every one of its NDA-era projects was approved under Congress. Most of the hill and north-eastern states above 1.5x were BJP- or NDA-governed when their loans were approved. The claim also miscounts the hill/north-eastern group as 7 of 11 when it is 8. If the ratios are joined to ruling party by approval date, they do not show the neutral mix the text describes. They lean NDA-aligned, and small-state denominators and pipeline timing explain that lean. So the defensible statement is "party cannot be separated from state size and timing on this lens", not "no party pattern". The claim as worded does not survive, and it needs correcting before it can stay analytic.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Change s from fin:ibrd to a World Bank Group node, or split the claim into IBRD and IDA. 2. Text: say "8 of 11 are hill/north-eastern (incl. Tripura), 3 southern", not 7. 3. Remove "southern opposition-run". Only Kerala was opposition-run throughout. AP is NDA-ally (TDP) for about 69% of its NDA-era approvals, including P507508 Amaravati (US$800m, 2024-12-19). TN is mixed (AIADMK, an NDA ally 2019-23, until May 2021). 4. Remove "(BJP-run)" for Chhattisgarh, since all of its NDA-era approvals (2019-2023) fell under the Congress government. Either code every state by ruling party at each approval date or drop party labels entirely. 5. Replace "no party pattern" with "the per-capita lens cannot separate party from state size and pipeline timing; above-1.5x states were mostly NDA/NEDA-governed at approval, and nearly all are small hill/NE states". 6. Report the UPA share as method-dependent (31% on the regex attribution, about 38% on the pre-fetched borrower/agency/title attribution) and state the exclusion rules (Dropped, pipeline, grant-only, multi-state). 7. Check Haryana's ratio against P510686 (US$300m, 2025-12-10). It gives about 0.61x, not below 0.6x. 8. Use the undivided AP population for UPA-era ratios. The symmetryCheck figure "AP 0.35x" conflicts with the US$1.7-1.8bn of AP-titled UPA approvals (P075174, P100789, P071250, P100954, etc.) and should be recomputed. 9. Add to upgradeIf: the Union Budget 2024-25 speech on multilateral finance for Amaravati, the one documented case where a Union statement ties a state's World Bank loan to political commitments.

verdicts.dateTest: Stated as a claim: the World Bank (IBRD and IDA) financed measures the Government of India (MoF/DEA) had already announced, 2020–23. The 2020 dates hold. PMGKY was announced 26 March 2020; the P173943 Program Document says "measures announced on March 25, 2020", a one-day difference. P173943 was approved 2020-05-14, and the PD itself is dated April 30, 2020. ECLGS was announced 13–17 May 2020 (PD: "The Program announced during May 13 - 17, 2020"), and the WB API shows P174292 approved 2020-06-30. MSME PA#5 is the RBI sandbox, "circular issued on August 13, 2019". PA#7 is PSB59, which the PD says was "Launched in November 2018". So for all three 2020 COVID operations the measures came before approval. The 2023 end of the window fails. The P181032 CCTS notification (Trigger #6) was issued 2023-06-28, one day before board approval, and was designed with Bank technical assistance (TA), so "already announced, not shaped by the Bank" does not hold for 2023.
verdicts.identityTest: The source node is wrong. s = fin:ibrd, but P173943 is IBRD US$200m plus IDA US$550m, and P174027 (US$400m) is IDA only. Of the roughly ₹14,288 cr of 2020 DPF money, about ₹7,107 cr is IDA, not IBRD. The target is correct: borrower India through DEA/MoF, and the MSME loan was signed by Addl Secy DEA S. K. Khare. Program Document IDs are correct.
verdicts.baseRate: Close to 100%. Under World Bank DPF policy, prior actions are by definition measures the borrower completes before Board presentation. Every DPF for every borrower, including UPA-era Indian DPLs such as the 2009 US$2bn Banking Sector Support DPL, has prior actions that predate approval. Showing that the prior actions predate approval therefore says nothing about who authored the policy. It is a definitional truism. The SPEC's UPA-vs-NDA control was not run.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. No party is accused. No World Bank or MoF statement on authorship was found, and none was asked for.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Bank's DPF instrument rewards completed government actions. In an emergency (2020) the Bank picked prior actions from GoI's announced COVID package. In programmatic series (2023) it co-designs reforms through analytical work and TA, then counts them as prior actions. Neither pattern shows capture in either direction.
verdicts.reason: The record's own killIf condition is met by a source the record itself cites. The P181032 Program Document (Low-Carbon DPL, 2023) says Bank TA "provided inputs to the National Green Hydrogen Roadmap, the NGHM", and lists underpinnings for PA #9 ("Supported BEE in designing the carbon market in India", through the partnership-for-market-readiness TA), PA #10 ("Supported SEBI to amend the existing regulations") and PA #11 ("Supported the MoF on the design of the Sovereign Green Bond Framework"). The MSME PD lists "IFC TA on Regulatory Sandbox" as the underpinning for PA#5. So "the Bank financed the package rather than dictating it" is refuted for 2023 and weakened for one 2020 action. "Dictating" is also a strawman: the documented middle case is Bank TA shaping measures that GoI then adopts. The claim's examples of the "real conditionality" (the SEBI ESG and carbon-market triggers) were themselves Bank-supported designs. The amount does not reconcile either. The file's own loan edges give 1,508 + 4,147 (P173943) + 2,960 (P174027) + 5,673 (P174292) = ₹14,288 cr, not ₹14,328 cr. Adding P181032 (₹12,431 cr) would give ₹26,719 cr, yet the text says "2020–23". Benefit confidence is marked "documented" for a total that no source states and that does not add up. What survives is a narrow analytic note: the three 2020 COVID operations financed measures already announced.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Restrict the scope to the 2020 COVID operations P173943, P174027 and P174292. Change text and lab from "2020–23" to "2020". Set to = 2020-12-15, not 2023-06-29. Drop the P181032 source, or move it to contra. (2) Replace "rather than dictating it" with "selected prior actions from measures GoI had already announced". Delete "forward triggers are the real conditionality". (3) Add a contra: the P181032 PD says Bank TA fed into the NGHM, the CCTS (via partnership-for-market-readiness TA), the SEBI amendments and the Sovereign Green Bond Framework, and the MSME PA#5 underpinning cites IFC TA to RBI on the sandbox. (4) Change amountCr from 14,328 to 14,288. (5) Change benefit.confidence from "documented" to "analytic", since it is a derived sum. (6) Change s from fin:ibrd to a World Bank node covering IBRD and IDA, or split the edge (IBRD ₹7,181 cr; IDA ₹7,107 cr). (7) Note that the P173943 PD dates PMGKY as "announced on March 25, 2020", while PIB gives 26 March. (8) Run the UPA-era DPL control (for example the 2009 Banking Sector Support DPL) before publication, or state that prior-action timing is non-discriminating. (9) Change upgradeIf, because "none found in the five PDs read" is contradicted by P181032.
